label: I q.18 a.3 co. — Intellectual life is more perfect through self-direction to ends
interpretation: The article grades life through self-operation: plants as to execution, animals also as to the form acquired through sense, and intellectual beings as to ordering to an end. In humans this is compatible with first principles and the ultimate end being fixed by nature. The highest case is argued separately, where nature is its very act of understanding.
attribution: The passage states that intellectual beings live in a more perfect manner because intellect enables them to direct themselves in relation to an end, which is the premise.
